messages:
hannah: Hey all, first day Fedora user here. I can reach internal IPs over WireGuard but the SSO redirect for the internal dashboard keeps bouncing to a public login and fails. Browser shows DNS for dashboard.corp.redwood resolves to 13.82.44.10 (public) instead of 10.45.5.12. Anyone seen systemd-resolved + split-tunnel weirdness?
diego: welcome! :wave: what does `resolvectl status` show for the wg0 link?
hannah: pasted small part: `Link 4 (wg0)
       Current Scopes: DNS
DefaultRoute setting: yes
       LLMNR setting: yes
MulticastDNS setting: no
  DNS Servers: 10.45.1.10
   DNS Domain: corp.redwood`
diego: hmm DNS server is set but maybe the search/suffix order makes your browser prefer public A record for the bare name. Try `resolvectl query dashboard.corp.redwood` from shell to see which IP returns.
hannah: `resolvectl query dashboard.corp.redwood` returns 10.45.5.12 locally, but `dig dashboard.corp.redwood` returns 13.82.44.10 (public) when run from a process that uses /etc/resolv.conf (like docker or some browsers on Fedora).
netops: Fedora often has multiple resolver layers: systemd-resolved, NetworkManager, and some apps use /etc/resolv.conf (which may point to NetworkManager stub) while others talk to resolved's DNS stub on 127.0.0.53. For split-tunnel we want the wg0 link to be the authoritative resolver for corp.redwood. Quick fixes:
1) `sudo resolvectl dns wg0 10.45.1.10` and `sudo resolvectl domain wg0 ~corp.redwood` (tilde makes it routing-only for that domain).
2) If apps ignore resolved, replace /etc/resolv.conf with a symlink to /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf: `sudo ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf` so all processes use resolved.
3) For Docker/containers, set DNS in daemon.json to 10.45.1.10.
hannah: applied option 1: resolvectl shows `DNS Domain: ~corp.redwood` and `resolvectl query dashboard.corp.redwood` now returns 10.45.5.12 for both shell and `dig` (I restarted NetworkManager). The dashboard SSO redirect now works.
diego: great! we'll add an onboarding note for Fedora users: ensure wg0 has `~corp.redwood` domain and that /etc/resolv.conf points to resolved. @it-support can you add this to the Linux setup doc and include the exact commands?
it-support: filing ONB-502: "Fedora/systemd-resolved: set wg0 domain and DNS for split-tunnel" and assigning to netops. We'll update the quickstart.
infra-bot: provisioned: user/hannah added to infra and docs groups
hannah: thanks everyone, smooth first-day win. Also, any recommended ~/.ssh/config snippets for jumping through bastion from Fedora?
diego: drop this in ~/.ssh/config:
```
Host *.corp.redwood
  ProxyJump %r@bastion-eu-1
  User %r
```
That uses your username and ProxyJump automatically for internal hosts.
hannah: added and tested `ssh git@repo.corp.redwood` works via bastion. Appreciate the help! :tada:
